page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based server instance powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 1890 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive; PassMark memory score and read-only large block memory bandwidth both rank in the top 10%. Database operations on PassMark also achieve top-tier status, and Redis SET operations register in the top 25%. However, single-core performance is average, and large-scale LLM inference is limited, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10%.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a compute-focused resource profile with a lower memory footprint, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require high parallel processing power without massive memory overhead. The combination of dedicated ARM cores, fast memory bandwidth, and local NVMe SSD storage makes it suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale language model inference.
